title: rubus ursinus subsp. vitifolius
intro: Rubus ursinus subsp. vitifolius, commonly known as the thimbleberry, is a subspecies of the thimbleberry plant that is native to the Pacific Northwest region of North America. This plant is valued for its edible fruit, which is rich in nutrients and antioxidants, providing health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, which may help protect against chronic diseases like cancer and heart disease. The therapeutic actions of Rubus ursinus subsp. vitifolius include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiviral properties, making it useful for treating wounds, infections, and other health conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include anthocyanins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
